# #1757: Patch: the pack-opening scene takes and returns focus and closes on Escape like the game's other dialogs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The pack-opening scene is a full-screen modal, but it ignores the keyboard: Escape does nothing, focus is never moved into it, Tab walks the inert page behind it, and its only exit — the Close button — is disabled while a pack is still opening, so a keyboard player whose open request stalls has no way out at all. After the change it behaves like every other overlay in the game: focus moves in, stays in, comes back out, and Escape closes it when closing is allowed.

## Why

`PackScene` is portalled to `document.body` with `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` (`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx:212-219`) but installs no keyboard or focus handling — no initial focus, no trap, no restore, no Escape — while every other overlay uses `useModalOverlay` (`apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts:150-207`) or hand-rolls the same (`settings/SettingsPanel.tsx:166-228`, `tutorial/TutorialResult.tsx:127-136`). Its Close button is disabled while `busy` (`PackOpening.tsx:316`), which a hung `openPack` request makes a real trap.

## Proposal

Wrap the scene in the shared overlay behaviour — focus on open, a Tab trap, focus restoration on close, and Escape honouring `busy` exactly as Close does.

## Where it lands

`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx`; the shared `useModalOverlay` behaviour in `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts` or its owning module; vitest beside the pack tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Focus enters the scene on open and returns to the opener on close
- [ ] Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog
- [ ] Escape closes it unless `busy` — matching the Close button's disabled state
- [ ] Mouse and reduced-motion behaviour are unchanged

## Size and risks

Small–medium — one component adopting an existing pattern; the only judgment is whether a hung open should offer a cancel, which the `busy` rule already answers.
